title: Async rendezvous layer for staggered NCCL overlap and per-stage kernel selection
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: reduce tail latency and improve effective throughput for heterogeneous multi-GPU prefill + decode workloads by introducing an asynchronous rendezvous layer that coordinates per-stage kernel selection and staggered NCCL windows. This ticket scopes a runtime component that decouples stage readiness signals from strict synchronous barriers and enables optimistic kernel swaps based on observed sequence-length distributions and attention tiling patterns.
background: Current approach forces tight inter-stage barriers for kernel selection and NCCL collective launches, which increases serialization in mixed batch workloads. Prior tickets explored topology-aware sharding and staged comm coordinators, but we still see 8-20% tail regressions on bursty short-sequence traffic when model variants switch kernels or when attention tiling differs between prefill and decode phases.
proposal: Implement an async rendezvous layer that: (1) publishes per-stage 'ready' tokens with metadata (seq_len_histogram, preferred_kernel_hint, kv_cache_state), (2) allows downstream stages to start NCCL launches opportunistically while upstream stages complete non-blocking work, and (3) supports a fallback deterministic barrier when consistency constraints require it. The layer will be pluggable so kernel-selection policy modules can subscribe and make local decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Tail p99 latency for mixed prefill+decode workload decreases by >=10% on 8-GPU A100 jobs compared to current mainline
End-to-end correctness preserved: generated outputs are bitwise-identical for deterministic kernel paths and statistically equivalent for optimized paths (regression tests pass)
No increase in intra-GPU memory spike >5% during overlap windows
Feature gated behind runtime flag and tested in canary fleet with rollback path
implementation_notes: Introduce rendezvous API surface: publish_ready(stage_id, metadata), await_window(stage_id, window_hint)
Metadata schema is intentionally minimal: sequence_length_buckets, preferred_kernel_label, kv_cache_prefix_hash
Non-blocking NCCL launches: use CUDA streams + IGP support where available; fall back to current barrier if launch fails
Kernel selection module will observe thoughtput and latency; initial policy = 'latency_pref' for short sequences, 'throughput_pref' for long sequences
Add metrics: rendezvous_wait_ms, opportunistic_nccllaunches, kernel_swaps_rate, rollback_triggers
Ensure compatibility with existing routing/fallback: rendezvous honors model-variant compatibility checks

experiment_results: Local sim: 16-card heterogeneous job (2xV100 + 6xA100) reduced p99 by 12% on mixed batches when opportunistic NCCL overlap was allowed
Small cluster (4xA100): for short-seq-heavy workload (median 16 tokens), throughput improved 9% and decoder-side kernel swaps increased resiliency without correctness loss
Edge case observed: when sequence-length histogram is bimodal and stage affinity differs, kernel selection churn increased; mitigated by adding 2s suppression window
risks: Increased nondeterminism for some optimized kernel paths could complicate reproducibility for customers in Private deployments
Aggressive overlap could amplify network congestion on certain NIC topologies—need to coordinate with topology-aware router
Complexity of rendezvous API may leak into per-model configs if not properly abstracted
rollout_plan: Feature flagged. Start with internal canary jobs running non-critical traffic. Monitor rendezvous metrics and errors for 72h before expanding to customer-facing Routing Policies. Provide immediate rollback by disabling opportunistic_nccl flag.
testing_plan: Unit tests for publish/await semantics; e2e deterministic workloads for correctness; A/B perf tests on canary fleet; fuzz test sequence histograms to detect kernel-churn edge cases.
